question.text: Under SEBI Circular dated October 21, 2021, the Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) of a Category III AIF shall be filed with SEBI:

answer.text: Directly by the Sponsor — no intermediary required.
Through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker who issues a due-diligence certificate.
Through the Custodian for safekeeping purposes.

explanation.text: The Logic: As per SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-I/DF6/P/CIR/2021/645 dated October 21, 2021, the PPM must be filed with SEBI through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker at the time of seeking registration or launching new schemes. The merchant banker conducts independent due diligence on disclosures and provides a due-diligence certificate. Intimations of specific PPM term changes (per SEBI Circular April 29, 2024) may be filed directly without merchant banker involvement. The Trap: Option A ignores the merchant-banker requirement. Option B confuses trustee duties with PPM filing. Option D swaps custodian and merchant banker roles. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D test the same merchant-banker filing rule. XIX-B (distributor) uses the PPM as key disclosure evidence. X-B (IA L2) references the PPM as pre-investment disclosure.
